 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 26.08.2011 Passed In Mvc
No.1077/2008 On The File Of The Presiding Officer,
Fast Track Court, Additional Mact, Hassan, Partly
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day

, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

1. This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellants-claimants, challenging the judgment and award dated 26.08.2011, passed in MVC No.1077/2008, on the file of Fast Track And Additional MACT at Hassan, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' NC: 2023:KHC:20790 for brevity) questioning the liability fixed on the owner of the motor cycle and also for enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts:
The appellants - claimants are the mother, son and daughter of deceased Sannegowda.

That on 31.01.2007 at about 11.30 p.m., near Haralahalli gate on Hassan Belur road, when the deceased Sannegowda was proceeding by walk, at that time the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA- 13/R-5207 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased Sannegowda.

Due to the impact, Sannegowda Deveeramma vs The Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159311764/
2 sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

entities.text: Sannegowda Deveeramma vs The Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellants- claimants under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation.
3. The deceased was an agriculturist and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
The appellants, who are the wife, son and daughter were depending upon the earning of the deceased.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on NC: 2023:KHC:20790 record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.4,93,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The Tribunal held respondent - owner of the offending vehicle if liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard the learned counsel for appellants and learned counsel for respondent No.1 and perused the material on record.
5.
The learned counsel appearing for the appellants- claimants submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening the liability on the owner of the vehicle.
It is further submitted that the motor cycle has dashed the deceased and deceased died in the accident.
The owner himself had come forward to the Tribunal and stated that he has seen the motor cycle which caused the accident.
On the basis of the evidence on record and on the basis of insurance policy, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation by indemnifying the owner.

Therefore, prays to shift the liability on the insurance company by NC: 2023:KHC:20790 holding both the owner of the offending vehicle and insurer as jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
He further argued for enhancement of compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that the offending motor cycle has not caused the accident and it is falsely implicated in this case for the purpose of making claim against the insurance company and therefore justified that the judgment and decree passed by the Tribunal in exonerating the insurance company for the reasons discussed in the judgment.
7. In the present case, the accident was caused on 31.01.2001 at 9.30 p.m.
It is alleged in the claim petition that the rider of offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13/R-5207 had caused the accident.
Respondent - owner of the offending motor cycle has stated that he has dashed the deceased.

P.W.2, who is said to be eye-witness had deposed that he had witnessed the accident, but after NC: 2023:KHC:20790 cross-examination it is revealed that he did not lodge complaint before the police and also he did not take the deceased - Sannegowda to the hospital from the scene of the accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal has doubted his evidence that there is no eye-witness.
If really P.W.2 was an eye-witness, then he would have lodged complaint before the police, but the complaint is given by some other person on the next day i.e., on 01.03.2007.
Even though P.W.2 had witnessed the accident, he did not take the deceased to the hospital.
The deceased and P.W.2 are residents of same village.
8. Further R.W.1, who is the owner of offending motor cycle has caused the accident.
The deceased and R.W.1 are residents of same village, but R.W.1 did not take the deceased to the hospital.
Therefore, this creates doubt regarding involvement of the motor cycle in the accident.

Therefore,
Deveeramma vs The Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159311764/
3

the Tribunal had observed that even though the deceased might have been hit by the vehicle and he has taken a 'U' turn, but doubted the involvement of the motor NC: 2023:KHC:20790 cycle in the accident belonging to respondent No.2.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly assessed that motor cycle is implicated to the accident only to claim against the insurance company since the owner of the offending vehicle was having insurance policy with respondent - insurance company.

Therefore,
respondent - owner of the offending vehicle, initially, during investigation denied the accident, but later he admitted in unequivocal terms regarding the cause of accident.
R.W.1 has been changing his version from time to time.
When the R.W.1 admitted that he has caused the accident, then he shall pay compensation to the claimants.
Therefore, regarding the liability, I do not see any reason to interfere with the judgment.
9. The Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.4,93,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
10. The learned counsel for the appellants-claimants submitted that the deceased was an agriculturist.

In the NC: 2023:KHC:20790 absence of any proof of income, notional income was taken at Rs.4,000/- per month and it is found to be just and correct, as the accident occurred in the year 2007.
11.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.
Vs. Delhi
Transport Corpn And Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104,
is '14', since the deceased was aged 45 years at the time of accident.
Further, the accident has occurred in the year 2007.
The notional income of deceased at Rs.4,000/- is to be taken into consideration.

Further, as per the principles law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% of his monthly income is added towards 'Loss Of Future Prospects In Life', i.e., Rs.1,000/- (Rs.4,000/- x 25%).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at Rs.5,000/- (Rs.4,000/- + Rs.1,000/-).
The deceased has three dependants.
Therefore, 1/3rd of deceased income is NC: 2023:KHC:20790 deducted towards personal and living expenses and the contribution to the family is taken as Rs.3,333/- per month.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss Of Dependency' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
Rs.3,333/- x 12 x 14 = Rs.5,59,999/-
(Rs.5,60,000/- = rounded off)
12.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards 'Loss of Estate' and Rs.10,000/- towards 'Funeral and Transportation Expenses', since the same is on lower side, the same is enhanced and a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under both heads.
13. The appellants - claimants are the wife, son and daughter of the deceased.

Therefore, as per the principles of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants - claimants are Deveeramma vs The Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159311764/
4 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20790 awarded Rs.40,000/- each, i.e., Rs.1,20,000/- under the head 'Loss of Consortium'.
14.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation awarded under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection' is set aside as the heads 'Loss of Consortium' and 'Loss of Love and Affection' are having more or less similar connotations.

15. Therefore, the appellants - claimants are entitled to the enhanced compensation as follows:
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 5,60,000/- 2 Transportation of dead body Rs. 15,000/- 3 Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
4 Loss of consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
TOTAL Rs. 7,10,000/-
16.
The appellants-claimants are entitled for a total enhanced compensation of Rs.7,10,000/- as against Rs.4,93,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the appellants are entitled for an additional Compensation of Rs.2,17,000/- (Rs.7,10,000 - Rs.4,93,000), along with - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20790 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
17.

Accordingly, I pass the following :
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award dated 26.08.2011, passed in MVC No.1077/2008, on the file of Fast Track and Additional MACT at Hassan is modified to the above extent.
iii.

The appellants are entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.2,17,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20790 of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
